Subject: Refurbished Vantorre CX-10: recurring E34 faults and warranty dispute

We purchased this refurbished Vantorre CX-10 (s/n VT21-30877) for $14,800 inc GST. It was delivered and commissioned on 14 September 2026. The listing stated that the steam generator had been descaled and pressure tested, and the core probe calibrated, with a six-month parts-and-labour warranty.

On 22 September, Kelsall attended for E34 steam-generator low-water-level faults and intermittent lockouts in combi and steam modes. The error log showed E34 nine times since delivery. The water-level sensor was replaced, inlet pressure was recorded as 320 kPa and OK, and three steam cycles passed testing. This visit was covered by warranty.

E34 returned four times during the following week. I also checked the core probe twice against a Thermapen in a lamb shoulder: the oven displayed 63°C while the Thermapen read 70°C on both tests.

At the 6 October service, the steam generator was reported as heavily scaled and was descaled and flushed. The probe was recalibrated to within one degree. Kelsall recommended a water softener and attributed the scale to our supply. However, our water utility advises that Fitzroy’s average hardness is approximately 15 mg/L as CaCO3, which is soft water. The oven had only been connected to our supply for three weeks when the heavy scale was found. Given that timeline and the advertised refurbishment, pre-existing scale or an underlying unit fault should be considered rather than attributing this solely to site water or operation.

On Saturday 24 October at 6:10pm, E34 locked us out during service with a full 60-cover booking. We finished the lamb on the stove and in our deck oven, removed pork belly from the menu and absorbed the resulting loss.

Dion attended again on 27 October and recorded E34 and further scale. Kelsall has classified this as a site-water issue outside warranty and invoiced a $280-plus-GST callout ($308 total), despite the unit being roughly six weeks old and within the advertised warranty period. We dispute that attribution and charge based on the figures and service history above.

Other kitchens considering a $15,000 refurbished combi should be aware of this fault sequence and warranty experience.
